title: Section-ring reconstruction and lax direct image form a coherent exact comparison
statement:
Fix a coefficient universe and sites $(C,J),(D,K)$ small relative to it [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Use tensor abelian sheaves with tensor the sheafification of sectionwise $\otimes_{\mathbf Z}$ [det-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor-structure], and assume sheafification exists and its local equivalences are monoidal. Let $F:C\to D$ be a functor for which precomposition sends $K$-sheaves to $J$-sheaves, and write $P_F H(V)=H(FV)$ for this direct image. Give $P_F$ its canonical lax monoidal structure induced by sheafification, with tensor and unit maps normalized by the actual sheafification units as in [lem-sfb-sheaf-pushforward-generator-comparison]. Let $R_C,R_D$ be commutative monoid objects in these tensor abelian-sheaf categories, and let $\psi:R_C\to P_FR_D$ be a morphism of monoid objects. Let $B_C,B_D$ be their reconstructed section-ring sheaves, and $E_C,E_D$ the fixed internal/sectionwise module equivalences [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence].

There is a unique morphism of ring sheaves $\phi_\psi:B_C\to P_FB_D$ whose additive map on sections is $\psi_V$ for every $V\in C$. Define $P^{\rm int}_{F,\psi}=\operatorname{Res}_\psi\operatorname{mapMod}(P_F)$ using [sk-def-sfb-transport, sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars], and define $P^{\rm sec}_{F,\phi_\psi}$ on sectionwise module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] by $(P^{\rm sec}N)(V)=N(FV)$ with action $r n=\phi_{\psi,V}(r)n$. There is a unique natural comparison
$$r_{F,\psi}:E_CP^{\rm int}_{F,\psi}\xrightarrow{\sim}P^{\rm sec}_{F,\phi_\psi}E_D$$
whose underlying sheaf map is the identity; its reconstructed section action is $r n=\psi_V(r)n$.

These comparisons are compatible with composition: for a third site $(H,L)$ satisfying the same size and sheafification assumptions, a functor $G:D\to H$ with the same sheaf-restriction property, a commutative monoid $R_H$, and $\theta:R_D\to P_GR_H$, let $K:C\to H$ be a functor with the same sheaf-restriction property together with a natural isomorphism $\kappa:K\xrightarrow{\sim}GF$ (for instance $K=GF$ and $\kappa=\mathrm{id}$), and let $c_\kappa:P_FP_G\xrightarrow{\sim}P_K$ be the induced isomorphism of abelian-sheaf direct images, $(c_\kappa H')(V)=H'(\kappa_V)$. Put $\chi=c_{\kappa,R_H}\circ P_F(\theta)\circ\psi:R_C\to P_KR_H$. Then $\phi_\chi=c_{\kappa,B_H}\circ P_F(\phi_\theta)\circ\phi_\psi$, and the square comparing $r_{K,\chi}$ with $P^{\rm sec}_{F,\phi_\psi}(r_{G,\theta})\circ r_{F,\psi}$ commutes using the internal and sectionwise direct-image compositors whose underlying sheaf isomorphism is $c_\kappa$. The identity-functor comparisons agree as well. Each $E_C$ and its quasi-inverse are additive exact equivalences: a sequence of internal module sheaves is exact if and only if its image under $E_C$ is exact, and conversely for the quasi-inverse.

proof.text:
Write $t_C(A,B):A\otimes_pB\to U_C(A\otimes B)$ and $u_C:\underline{\mathbf Z}\to U_C\mathbf1_C$ for the actual sheafification units, and similarly on the other sites. By [det-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor-structure] and [def-weil-pbc-sheafification], a sheaf map out of $A\otimes B$ is determined by precomposition with $t_C(A,B)$. By [det-def-sfb-ring-object-transport], for a monoid $S$ on $D$ the multiplication on $P_FS$ is $P_F(m_S)\circ\mu_F$ and its unit is $P_F(e_S)\circ e_F$. Applying [lem-sfb-sheaf-pushforward-generator-comparison] gives
$$U_C(P_Fm_S\circ\mu_F)\circ t_C(P_FS,P_FS)=P_F(U_Dm_S\circ t_D(S,S)),$$
and the analogous unit equation with $u_C,u_D$. If $S$ is commutative, the resulting section products commute; the multiplication and its composite with symmetry therefore agree after $t_C$, hence agree as sheaf maps. Thus $P_FS$ is commutative. For such $S$, reconstruction as in [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence] gives precisely the section ring $V\mapsto B_S(FV)$: the product of $a,b\in S(FV)$ is their original product and its unit is $1\in S(FV)$. This uses the generator formula, not preservation of tensor products by evaluation.

source.place: Tag 03D6, definition-pushforward; agent-written tensor reconstruction using the normalized generator comparison

proof.text: The monoid-map equations [sk-def-sfb-ring-object] for $\psi$ imply on the tensor generator $r\otimes s$ that $\psi_V(rs)=\psi_V(r)\psi_V(s)$, by Step 1, and on the unit generator $1$ that $\psi_V(1)=1$. Its components are already additive and commute with restriction. Hence they define a morphism of ring sheaves $\phi_\psi:B_C\to P_FB_D$. A ring-sheaf morphism with these additive components must coincide at every section with this one, so is unique. In particular no change of coefficient rings is implicit in the notation $P_FB_D$.

source.place: Tag 03D6, definition-pushforward; ring map underlying restriction of scalars

proof.text:
For an internal $R_D$-module $M$ with action $a_M:R_D\otimes M\to M$, [sk-def-sfb-transport] and clause 1 of [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars] give the internal pushforward action
$$P_F(a_M)\circ\mu_{F,R_D,M}\circ(\psi\otimes1).$$
Precompose with $t_C(R_C,P_FM)$. Naturality of the sheafification unit [det-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor-structure, def-weil-pbc-sheafification] first moves $\psi\otimes1$ to the sectionwise tensor; [lem-sfb-sheaf-pushforward-generator-comparison] then replaces $\mu_F\circ t_C$ by the restricted $t_D$. Thus the reconstructed action on $r\in R_C(V)$ and $n\in M(FV)$ is exactly
$$a_{M,FV}\bigl(t_{D,R_D,M,FV}(\psi_V(r)\otimes n)\bigr)=\psi_V(r)n.$$
The reconstruction convention is that of [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence].

source.place: Tag 03D6, definition-pushforward; action by restriction via the coefficient ring map

proof.text: By [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], the sectionwise pushforward has the same underlying sheaf and the same action as Step 3. Its semilinear restriction law follows explicitly from naturality: for $v:V'\to V$, restriction of $\psi_V(r)n$ is $\psi_{V'}(r|_{V'})\,(n|_{FV'})$. A morphism $h:M\to M'$ acts at $V$ by $h_{FV}$ on both sides, and is linear because $h_{FV}(\psi_V(r)n)=\psi_V(r)h_{FV}(n)$. Thus the identity maps of the underlying sheaves define a natural comparison $r_{F,\psi}$. They and their identities in the reverse direction are module maps, so the comparison is invertible. Any comparison with underlying identity has these very components, and is unique.

source.place: Tag 03D6, definition-pushforward; underlying abelian sheaf and restricted module action

proof.text:
The map $c_{\kappa,A}(V)=A(\kappa_V)$ is natural in $A$ and $V$, and has inverse $A(\kappa_V^{-1})$. It is monoidal for the normalized lax structures. Indeed precompose
$$c_{\kappa,A\otimes B}\circ P_F(\mu_G)\circ\mu_F=\mu_K\circ(c_{\kappa,A}\otimes c_{\kappa,B})$$
with $t_C(P_FP_GA,P_FP_GB)$. Twice [lem-sfb-sheaf-pushforward-generator-comparison] turns the left side at $V$ into $(A\otimes B)(\kappa_V)\circ t_{H,GFV}$. Naturality of $t_C$ and the comparison for $K$ turn the right side into $t_{H,KV}\circ(A(\kappa_V)\otimes B(\kappa_V))$. These are equal by presheaf naturality of the sheafification unit [det-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor-structure, def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. The same calculation on $u_C$ reduces the unit equation to $\mathbf1_H(\kappa_V)u_{H,GFV}=u_{H,KV}$, since the constant presheaf restriction is the identity. Unique extension under sheafification proves both equations. By [det-def-sfb-ring-object-transport], $c_\kappa$ takes the transported monoid structure to the $P_K$ structure, and $\chi=c_{\kappa,R_H}P_F(\theta)\psi$ is a monoid morphism.

source.place: Steps 1–2, coherent direct images; agent-written general-site compositor calculation

proof.text:
Apply Step 2 also to $\theta$ and $\chi$. At every $V$, the additive component of the claimed composite ring map is
$$R_H(\kappa_V)\circ\theta_{FV}\circ\psi_V=\chi_V.$$
Here $B_H(\kappa_V)$ has precisely the underlying additive map $R_H(\kappa_V)$ by reconstruction [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence]. The composite is a ring map: restriction maps of $B_H$ and the maps $\phi_\theta,\phi_\psi$ are ring homomorphisms. Uniqueness in Step 2 proves $\phi_\chi=c_{\kappa,B_H}\circ P_F(\phi_\theta)\circ\phi_\psi$.

source.place: Steps 1–2, coefficient-map compatibility needed for composition of module direct images

proof.text:
For an internal $R_H$-module $N$, Steps 3–4 identify the twice-pushed action at $V$ with $r n=\theta_{FV}(\psi_V(r))n$ on $N(GFV)$, and the singly-pushed action with $r n'=\chi_V(r)n'$ on $N(KV)$. Naturality of the reconstructed module restrictions [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] gives
$$N(\kappa_V)\bigl(\theta_{FV}(\psi_V(r))n\bigr)=R_H(\kappa_V)\bigl(\theta_{FV}(\psi_V(r))\bigr)\,N(\kappa_V)(n)=\chi_V(r)N(\kappa_V)(n).$$
Thus $c_{\kappa,N}$ is linear for these two actions. Its inverse is linear too: substitute $n=c_{\kappa,N}^{-1}(n')$ into this equation and apply the inverse. By the full faithfulness of [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence], these maps give the internal compositor as well as the sectionwise one. All paths around the asserted comparison square send $n$ to $N(\kappa_V)(n)$; equality of section maps proves its commutativity. For $F=\mathrm{id}$ and $\psi=\mathrm{id}$, the same formula is the original action, and every comparison is the identity. The identity instances of the composition square therefore agree as well.

source.place: Steps 1–2, explicit compatibility of internal and sectionwise direct-image compositors and identity comparisons

proof.text: The equivalence $E_C$ preserves addition on morphisms [def-weil-pbc-additive-functor]: both module categories add underlying abelian-sheaf maps, and reconstruction leaves those maps unchanged [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence]. If $Q_C$ is its quasi-inverse and $\epsilon:E_CQ_C\xrightarrow{\sim}1$, then $E_C(Q_C h)=\epsilon_Y^{-1}h\epsilon_X$. Additivity of $E_C$ and bilinearity of composition make the right side additive in $h$; faithfulness of $E_C$ implies $Q_C(h+h')=Q_C(h)+Q_C(h')$. This covers any fixed quasi-inverse, even when its underlying sheaves are only canonically isomorphic to the original ones.

source.place: Step 1, additive comparison of the internal and sectionwise module categories

proof.text: The category of abelian sheaves is abelian [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. By [det-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor-closed], its sheafified tensor is additive in each variable and $R_C\otimes-$ preserves finite colimits. Hence [lem-sfb-modobj-abelian] applies to the internal module category; the sectionwise module category is abelian by [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], since the site is small in the coefficient universe. Apply clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-equivalence-injective-resolutions] to the additive equivalence $E_C$ and, separately, to its additive quasi-inverse from Step 8. They preserve kernels, cokernels and exact sequences, and are exact in the finite-limit/finite-colimit sense of [def-galois-exact-functor]. If an image sequence is exact, applying the quasi-inverse and then the equivalence unit gives an isomorphic exact original sequence. The converse follows by applying $E_C$. Interchanging $E_C$ and its quasi-inverse proves the last assertion in both directions, on every site in the statement.
